task_specification.objective: Deliver a readable Alpha combat slice in which M4 enemies use credible rifle motion and every authoritative shot, damage, kill, death, and mission transition produces synchronized, independently routed visual, HUD, camera, and audio evidence, while preserving clean boot, the intact authored industrial map, player movement, and accepted viewmodel behavior.

diagnosis.root_cause: The live enemy presentation binds an intact M4 to pistol idle, aim, fire, and reload clips, so the defect is semantic animation-profile incompatibility rather than another transform problem. Combat and mission presentation are also fragmented across observers: mission audio aliases unrelated roles through one generated family-tone player, required footstep/dialogue/ambience/music layers are absent, and the combat-feedback channels lack one event-ID-joined receipt; the HUD additionally listens for `enemy_death` while mission authority emits `enemy_died`, preventing the required kill row from reliably observing the lethal event.

stop_conditions: Stop and report an animation-source compatibility blocker if neither existing authored motion library contains credible rifle clips and no legally sourced intact compatible motion package can be provisionally bound; never relabel pistol motion as rifle motion, edit imported GLB internals, or compensate with per-bone/per-mesh transforms.

Reject any feedback implementation that lets HUD, audio, VFX, animation, or instrumentation create damage, ammo, score, capture, countdown, or terminal state, or that replaces the authoritative event ID with channel-local identities.
Do not expand this iteration into the deferred bomb-finale, replay-cache, performance-qualification, opening-CG, cloud/sun-flare, world-density, product-shell, or map-layout work.
Stop the implementation pass if project parsing, resource loading, or `clean_boot` regresses; repair that regression before further presentation work.

Do not claim issue or phase closure from source inspection, snapshots, or Developer self-validation. Formal closure requires fresh host/Tester runtime evidence and passing verdicts for all three required checks.

strategy.rationale: Change strategy after two no-progress rounds: isolate defects at semantic adapter boundaries instead of repeating transform or cosmetic tuning. First bind weapon-compatible motion to the preserved enemy rig. Then join existing presentation listeners by immutable event identity, repair the lethal-event kind mismatch, and add distinct resource/bus routing plus bounded receipts so Tester can recapture the complete matrix. This prioritizes fresh product defects and missing player-facing audio behavior without reopening preserved packages or deferred work.

code: Load every changed script, scene, animation resource, audio stream, and bus layout without parse, missing-resource, cyclic-signal, or invalid-node-path errors; retain `validate:clean_boot` pass.

Audit the enemy motion profile so every configured clip exists in its bound AnimationPlayer, M4 core states contain no pistol substitutions, imported GLB files remain unchanged, and snapshots expose the resolved profile/clip.

Exercise deterministic event-contract checks showing that presenters only observe authority, preserve the originating ID, accept `enemy_died`, reject duplicate presentation, and never submit damage, ammo, score, capture, countdown, or result.

Verify every required audio role resolves to a non-silent stream and independent route, with bounded concurrency/lifetime and reset behavior; a stream assignment or `play()` call alone is insufficient without the runtime voice receipt.
runtime: Host/Tester: start a fresh ordinary-input Alpha encounter and retain paired advancing samples for enemy idle/walk/run, aim window, fire, reload, hurt, lethal hit, death, and cleanup. Each sample must include semantic state, resolved clip, normalized time, root/velocity, ground contact, weapon attachment, muzzle/shot ID, and two rendered frames.

Host/Tester: freeze/step one authoritative event at a time for player and enemy blocked shot, miss, hit, near miss, light/heavy/critical player damage, enemy nonlethal hit, kill, and death. For each ID capture before/during/after state, audio/VFX timeline, camera/damage mask, animation, health/ammo/score, combat row, and cleanup; all relevant channels must observe within two rendered frames.

Host/Tester: retain a mission-mix timeline covering deployment dialogue over ambience/music, player walk/sprint/crouch/landing on at least two encountered surfaces, one moving enemy footstep sequence, capture start/contest/interruption/completion, key/route unlock, one defusal stage, and a countdown warning. Confirm distinct roles, buses, waveform onsets, lifetimes, attenuation, priority, and no—.
visual: Enemy motion: use the shipped gameplay view for locomotion, aim, fire, reload, hurt, and death; add only one close-up where needed to judge support-hand contact, stock/shoulder relationship, muzzle alignment, foot planting, or clipping. Reject pistol posture, one-handed rifle presentation, frozen poses, socket drift, or sliding.

Combat feedback: compare compact muzzle/tracer/impact scale against the human silhouette and nearby industrial geometry; effects must reveal the hit surface and target rather than covering either. Damage uses a directional bounded red edge treatment, never a full-screen red/black mask.

HUD/reference alignment: show the actual top-right combat feed with a restrained yellow player-kill row, no bare `Enemy killed` label, broad opaque card, debug telemetry, or reticle/target occlusion. Mission/story text remains glyph-led and borderless.

Preservation: representative Alpha gameplay frames must retain the intact authored industrial environment, neutral daylight, contact shadows, readable materials, exact mouse-look/viewmodel framing, and unobstructed combat sightlines.

done_when: Every live M4-equipped enemy resolves idle/ready, aim, fire, and reload through rifle-compatible authored clips; no core M4 state uses pistol-labeled or visibly one-handed motion.
